title: Building JSON API Endpoints
learning_outcomes: Explain what building json api endpoints contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: json responses.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: API integrations cross a network boundary where responses can be slow, malformed, unauthorized, duplicated, or unavailable. Check status and content, set timeouts, and make retries and webhook processing safe to repeat. In this lesson, focus on json responses; then compare it with http status codes. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use building json api endpoints when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: API integrations cross a network boundary where responses can be slow, malformed, unauthorized, duplicated, or unavailable. Check status and content, set timeouts, and make retries and webhook processing safe to repeat. For building json api endpoints, begin with json responses. Also distinguish http status codes; request-body parsing; response structure. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
